title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Ralph went to the store and bought \(12\) pairs of socks for a total of \(\$24\). Some of the socks he bought cost \(\$1\) a pair, some of the socks he bought cost \(\$3\) a pair, and some of the socks he bought cost \(\$4\) a pair. If he bought at least one pair of each type, how many pairs of \(\$1\) socks did Ralph buy?

solutions.text:
Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be the numbers of \(\$1,\) \(\$3,\) and \(\$4\) pairs, respectively. Then \[a+b+c=12,\] \[a+3b+4c=24.\]

Subtracting gives \(2b+3c=12.\) Since at least one pair of each type was bought, \(b>0\) and \(c>0.\) Also \(3c<12,\) so \(c<4.\) Modulo \(2,\) the equation gives \(c\) even, so \(c=2.\)

Then \(2b+6=12,\) so \(b=3,\) and \(a=12-3-2=7.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the numbers of \(\$1,\) \(\$3,\) and \(\$4\) pairs be variables.
Subtract the pair-count equation from the cost equation.
